domain: Busan and the southeast coast (seaside / Kamakura-like side of the trip)
research_notes: Verified live in Oct 2026 from official pages: Blueline Park fares and October hours (bluelinepark.com), Spa Land Centum price and hours (shinsegae.com), Songdo cable car fares and hours (busanaircruise.co.kr), Hurshimchung 2026 reopening and prices (daily.hankooki.com, visitbusan), Gwangalli drone show October 2026 programme (busan.com, 28 Sep 2026), October 2026 Busan festival list (ontrip.kr), BIFF 2026 and Busan Fireworks 2026 dates. The session's web-search quota ran out partway through, so many hours and admission prices for free or cheap sights come from 2024-2025 knowledge and are marked medium or low confidence. Hotel prices are aggregator snapshots (hotelscombined.co.kr, Oct 2026 dates unless noted) for a 2-person base room. Prices for 3 adults are estimates built from those snapshots.

places.name: Haeundae Blueline Park Sky Capsule (Mipo - Cheongsapo)
places.summary: Small private pastel pods that run on an elevated rail 7-10 m above the old Donghae Nambu coastal railway. They carry 2-4 riders from Mipo to Cheongsapo at about 4 km/h, roughly 30 minutes one way, with the sea right below.
places.why: The closest Busan match to the Enoden coastal train in Kamakura: a slow ride along the sea past fishing villages and lighthouses. One capsule fits all 3 travelers.
places.autumn_note: October is shoulder season: clear, dry air with good visibility and less heat-haze than summer. Late-afternoon departures catch golden light on Cheongsapo's twin lighthouses.
places.time_needed: 30 min ride + 1.5-2.5 h combined with the Beach Train and Cheongsapo
places.hours: October (shoulder season, also Mar/Apr): 08:30-18:30. Hours can shift on busy weekends and holidays. Normal rain does not stop service; extreme weather does.
places.cost_note: Price is per capsule, one way. Official regular fares: 2 riders 50,000; 3 riders 55,000 (about 18,300 each); 4 riders 60,000. Discounted resident/senior fares (40k/45k/50k) do not apply to foreigners. No round-trip fare is listed. Package of Sky Capsule one way + Beach Train all-stations is 103,000 for 3 adults (55,000 + 3 x 16,000), so no saving over buying separately. Some blogs quote older or discounted prices of 30-45k; trust the official site.
places.booking: Official site bluelinepark.com (Korean UI; checkout may need Korean phone verification), at the Mipo or Cheongsapo ticket office on the day, or via Klook, KKday or Trip.com, which foreigners can use easily. Book as soon as the target date opens: an unverified 2026 blog says bookings open weekly about 4 weeks ahead (Tuesdays 07:00). Weekend and holiday slots sell out; weekday mornings are the easiest.
places.tips: Ride Mipo to Cheongsapo by capsule, walk Cheongsapo and its Daritdol Skywalk, then take the Beach Train on to Songjeong (or back). Sit facing the sea; the right side heading east. Bring the booking QR, and arrive 10-15 min before the slot. During BTS-concert week (Jun 2026) the park ran a promo with 3-4 riders at the 2-rider price, so watch for similar promos.

places.name: Haeundae Blueline Park Beach Train (Mipo - Songjeong)
places.area: Mipo - Dalmaji Tunnel - Cheongsapo - Daritdol Skywalk - Gudeokpo - Songjeong
places.summary: Tram-like sightseeing train with sideways sea-facing seats. It runs 4.8 km along the coast with 7 stops from Mipo (Haeundae) to Songjeong Beach, and you can hop on and off.
places.why: The second half of the Enoden analog: hop off at Cheongsapo (fishing village and lighthouses), Daritdol Skywalk and Gudeokpo, then finish at the surf beach in Songjeong, much like Enoden ending at Enoshima and Shichirigahama.
places.autumn_note: Comfortable October temperatures, roughly 15-22 C. The sun sets around 17:45 in late October, so aim for a 16:00-17:00 run.
places.time_needed: About 25-30 min end to end, or 2-3 h with stops
places.hours: October: departures from Mipo and from Songjeong 09:00-19:30. Times may change on weekends and holidays.
places.cost_note: Official: single ride 10,000 boarding at Mipo or Songjeong, 8,000 boarding at Cheongsapo or other intermediate stops; 2-ride ticket 14,000; all-stations hop-on pass 16,000.
places.booking: Same as the Sky Capsule: bluelinepark.com, station counters, Klook/KKday. It sells out less often than the capsule, but time slots fill on weekends.
places.tips: The all-stations pass makes sense if you want to stop at Cheongsapo and Daritdol. Some Visit Busan Pass versions have included the beach train in the past; check before buying separately.

places.name: Cheongsapo Village, Twin Lighthouses and Daritdol Skywalk
places.summary: Small fishing harbour between Haeundae and Songjeong, known for red and white twin lighthouses, grilled clam shacks, cafes and a glass-floored skywalk out over the rocks.
places.why: Feels like the small fishing coves near Kamakura and Enoshima: low-key, salty air, seafood and sea-view cafes.
places.autumn_note: October is a good month for grilled shellfish (jogae-gui) here.
places.hours: Village open always. The Daritdol skywalk is roughly 09:00-18:00 (2024-25 info; unverified for 2026).
places.closed: Skywalk may close in bad weather
places.cost_note: Free. Grilled clam platters for 3 people run about 50,000-70,000 KRW (2025 level).
places.tips: Reach it by Sky Capsule or Beach Train; bus 2 or 141 from Haeundae as a fallback.

places.name: Dalmaji-gil (Moontan Road)
places.summary: Winding cliff road above Mipo with sea-view cafes, galleries and the Haewoljeong pavilion. A boardwalk trail (Moontan-ro) runs through the pines.
places.why: A calm, upscale counterpart to the Shibuya-like bustle of Haeundae, similar to the hilltop cafe roads around Kamakura and Hayama.
places.autumn_note: Cherry trees here turn red-orange in late October to November, earlier than Busan's mountain foliage.
places.hours: Always open
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Walk up from Mipo or take a taxi to Haewoljeong, then walk down to Cheongsapo through the forest boardwalk.

places.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
places.summary: Buddhist temple built right on the seaside rocks (claims a 1376 founding), with a large Haesu Gwaneum statue, zodiac statues and stairs leading down to halls above crashing waves.
places.why: The seaside-temple answer to Kamakura's Hase-dera: temple, ocean views and pilgrims in one compact visit.
places.autumn_note: Clear October air. Visit at sunrise (about 06:40 late Oct) to beat the tour-bus crowds; the temple faces east over the sea.
places.hours: About 05:00 to sunset (around 19:00); 2024-25 info, unverified for 2026
places.cost_note: Free entry. The car park is paid (about 3,000 KRW).
places.tips: Very crowded late morning to afternoon, especially at weekends. From Haeundae: bus 139 or 181, or Donghae Line to OSIRIA station plus about 20 min walk or a short taxi. Pair with the Lotte Premium Outlet / Ananti Cove nearby. The approach is lined with snack stalls.

places.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village and Jeollyeong Coastal Walk
places.summary: White cliffside houses stacked above the sea on Yeongdo, with narrow lanes, cafes looking over the anchored ships, a seaside tunnel and a coastal walk below. Film set for 'The Attorney'.
places.why: Probably the most Kamakura-like neighbourhood in Busan: small lanes, cafes and the ocean at every turn, much like the cliffside lanes of Enoshima.
places.autumn_note: Sunset over the anchored ships is spectacular in October and the weather is mild.
places.hours: Village always open; cafes about 10:00-19:00. Many shops close one weekday, often Monday or Tuesday.
places.closed: Village none. Residents live here, so keep quiet.
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Combine with Taejongdae (10 min taxi) and the Samjin Eomuk flagship on Yeongdo. Bus 7, 71 or 508 from Nampo.

places.name: Taejongdae Park
places.summary: Wooded headland of sea cliffs with a lighthouse, the Sinseon rock platform, an observatory and a 4.3 km loop road served by the Danubi road train.
places.why: The rugged-nature counterpart to Izu's coastal cliffs.
places.autumn_note: Evergreen forest, so little foliage colour, but cool weather makes the loop walk pleasant.
places.hours: Park roughly 04:00-24:00. Danubi train about 09:30-17:30 (2024-25 info).
places.closed: Danubi may not run in bad weather; no fixed closing day confirmed
places.cost_note: Park entry free. Danubi road train about 4,000 KRW for adults (2024-25 price, unverified for 2026). Walking the loop is free.
places.booking: Danubi tickets on site only; queues form at weekends
places.tips: Walk down to the lighthouse and Sinseon rock. Bus 8, 30, 66 or 101 from Nampo or Busan Station.

places.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
places.summary: Hillside settlement of postwar refugees, painted in pastel colours, with art installations, small galleries, a 'Little Prince' photo spot and maze-like alleys.
places.why: Colourful stair-and-alley wandering, but busier and more touristy than Huinnyeoul. If you only have time for one, Huinnyeoul feels more like Kamakura.
places.autumn_note: No particular seasonal feature.
places.hours: Village always open; shops and info centre about 09:00-18:00 (Nov-Feb to 17:00)
places.cost_note: Free; the stamp map is about 2,000 KRW
places.tips: Take a taxi or maeul bus 1-1, 2 or 2-2 up from Toseong station (Line 1) and walk downhill. Go before 10:00 or late afternoon.

places.name: Oryukdo Skywalk
places.summary: Glass-floored horseshoe platform on a 35 m cliff overlooking the Oryukdo islets, at the meeting point of the East Sea and the South Sea. Southern start of the Igidae coastal walk.
places.why: A short, dramatic seaside viewpoint to pair with the Igidae walk.
places.autumn_note: Late October is the end of the season for the cosmos and silver grass on the Oryukdo Haemaji Park slope beside the skywalk (2025 pattern).
places.closed: Closes in rain, strong wind and snow
places.cost_note: Free; shoe covers provided
places.tips: Bus 27 or 131 from Kyungsung Univ/Pukyong station. Start here and walk north on Igidae toward Gwangalli.

places.name: Igidae Coastal Walk (Galmaet-gil section 2)
places.summary: About 4.7 km of cliffside boardwalks, suspension bridges and rocky coves from Oryukdo Skywalk to Dongsaengmal, with continuous views of Gwangan Bridge and the Haeundae skyline.
places.why: Matches the coastal hiking of the Izu peninsula, but ends at a city skyline, mixing nature and the bustling city.
places.autumn_note: October is the best month for it: cool and dry. Some silver grass grows on the headlands.
places.hours: Daylight hours advised
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Walk south to north (Oryukdo to Dongsaengmal) so the Gwangan Bridge view is ahead of you, then continue to Gwangalli for dinner and the night view. Wear proper shoes; there are many stairs.

places.name: Gwangalli Beach and Gwangan Bridge
places.summary: Urban beach facing the lit-up Gwangan suspension bridge, lined with bars, cafes and raw-fish restaurants. Busan's liveliest night-time waterfront.
places.why: Shibuya energy meets the seaside: buzzing at night with a light show over the water.
places.autumn_note: The drone show season continues on Saturdays. The Busan Fireworks Festival here is on Nov 7 2026, after the trip.
places.hours: Bridge lighting nightly (about sunset to midnight)
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Millak Waterfront Park and the Millak raw fish centre are at the north end. Metro Line 2 to Gwangan or Geumnyeonsan station.

places.name: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
places.summary: Free show of about 1,100 drones over Gwangalli Beach every Saturday, roughly 12 minutes per show. Oct-Feb times are 19:00 and 21:00.
places.why: A one-of-a-kind neon-and-sky spectacle, the Busan equivalent of a Shibuya night.
places.autumn_note: October 2026 programme: Oct 17 'Dimensional Station' with lasers; Oct 24 'Forest's Melody' (enchanted-forest theme with a violin-playing fox). Only Oct 24 is realistic for this trip, since Oct 17 is arrival day in Incheon.
places.hours: Saturdays 19:00 and 21:00 (Oct-Feb)
places.closed: Cancelled in bad weather or strong wind
places.cost_note: Free
places.booking: None; arrive 30 min early for a beach spot in the centre
places.tips: Watch from the sand in front of 219 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro, or book a restaurant or hotel room with a bridge view. The 21:00 show is less crowded.

places.name: BUSAN X the SKY (Haeundae LCT Landmark Tower observatory)
places.summary: Observatory on floors 98-100 of the 411 m LCT tower, with views over Haeundae beach, Gwangan Bridge and the coastline, plus a high-altitude cafe.
places.why: The Shibuya Sky equivalent of Busan.
places.autumn_note: Clear October days give long visibility; aim for sunset (about 17:45 late Oct).
places.hours: About 10:00-21:00, last entry 20:30 (2024-25 info, unverified for 2026)
places.cost_note: Adult about 27,000 KRW (2024-25 price); usually cheaper on Klook. Included in some Visit Busan Pass versions. Unverified for 2026: official site would not load.
places.booking: Walk up, official site busanxthesky.com, or Klook/KKday
places.tips: Skip it if you already do the Seoul Sky / N Seoul Tower, or if a sea-view hotel room already gives you the view.

places.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
places.summary: Korea's largest seafood market on the Nampo harbour front. Pick live fish downstairs and have it cut and served as hoe (sashimi) at an upstairs restaurant.
places.why: The Tsukiji-style counterpart for sushi-omakase lovers: the freshest raw fish in Busan, eaten on the spot.
places.autumn_note: Autumn favourites: jeon-eo (gizzard shad), galchi (hairtail) and flatfish. The Jagalchi Festival is usually in October (2025: Oct 23-26), but 2026 dates are unconfirmed.
places.hours: Roughly 05:00-22:00. Individual stalls and floors vary.
places.closed: The main Jagalchi Market building historically closes on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month (Oct 20 2026 is a 3rd Tuesday). Unverified for 2026.
places.cost_note: Assorted hoe for 3 is about 60,000-120,000 KRW plus a 4,000-5,000 KRW per-person table and side-dish charge.
places.tips: Agree on the price and weight before the fish is cut. Pair with BIFF Square and Gukje Market, both 5 min away.

places.name: BIFF Square, Gukje Market and Bosu-dong Book Alley
places.summary: Old-downtown market district: the film-festival plaza with ssiat hotteok (seed-stuffed pancake) and eomuk stalls, plus the sprawling postwar Gukje Market and the Kkangtong night market.
places.why: Retro, crowded and full of street food: the Ameyoko-style side of Busan.
places.autumn_note: BIFF 2026 runs Oct 6-15, so it ends before this trip.
places.hours: Shops about 09:00-20:00; street food until about 22:00
places.closed: Many Gukje stalls close on the 1st and 3rd Sunday (pattern before 2026, unverified)
places.cost_note: Free; ssiat hotteok about 2,000-2,500 KRW
places.tips: Combine with Jagalchi, Yongdusan Park / Busan Tower and the Songdo cable car.

places.name: Haeundae Traditional Market
places.summary: Short covered market street near Haeundae station with tteokbokki, eomuk, fried snacks, grilled eel and seafood.
places.why: An easy street-food dinner near the Haeundae hotels.
places.autumn_note: Busy in the evenings.
places.hours: About 09:00-23:00; varies by stall
places.cost_note: Snacks 3,000-15,000 KRW
places.tips: Sangguk-ine (상국이네) for tteokbokki and eomuk is a long-time favourite.

places.name: Jeonpo Cafe Street and Seomyeon
places.summary: Former tool-shop alleys turned into dozens of indie cafes, bakeries and bars, next to Seomyeon, Busan's main downtown nightlife and shopping hub with its underground malls, pocha (tent bars) and the Seomyeon Market dwaeji gukbap (pork soup) alley.
places.why: The closest thing to Shibuya and Shimokitazawa in Busan: neon, youth crowds and late nights.
places.autumn_note: The Jeonpo Coffee Festival is on Oct 17-18 2026 (opening day = arrival day in Incheon; Sunday Oct 18 is only possible if already in Busan).
places.hours: Cafes about 11:00-22:00; Seomyeon bars until late
places.closed: Many cafes close one weekday, often Monday
places.cost_note: Coffee 5,000-8,000 KRW
places.tips: Metro Line 1/2 Seomyeon station; Jeonpo station on Line 2. Dwaeji gukbap alley is at Seomyeon Market.

places.name: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car) and Songdo Skywalk
places.summary: 1.62 km cable car crossing the bay from Songdo Beach to Amnam Park, with optional glass-floor 'Crystal' cabins. The Songdo Cloud Trail sea walkway is beside it.
places.why: A playful seaside ride, much like the Enoshima-area attractions.
places.autumn_note: The night views are good in October.
places.hours: October: 09:00-21:00; ticket sales close 30 min before
places.closed: No regular closing day listed; stops in high wind
places.cost_note: Official, round trip adult: Air Cruise (standard) 19,000; Crystal Cruise (glass floor) 24,000
places.booking: On site, busanaircruise.co.kr, or Klook (usually discounted)
places.tips: Near the Fairfield by Marriott Songdo Beach. 15 min taxi from Nampo/Jagalchi.

places.name: Hurshimchung Spa (Dongnae Hot Springs, Hotel Nongshim)
places.summary: Natural hot-spring bathhouse attached to Hotel Nongshim, said to be the largest in Asia: about 40 baths under a glass dome, including cave, cypress and open-air baths. Fed by the 1,300-year-old Dongnae hot spring. Renovated for about 2 months; full operation resumed 1 May 2026.
places.why: The closest thing in the city to a traditional onsen soak; Dongnae has been Busan's hot-spring town since the Silla era. Bathing is single-sex and nude, as at Japanese onsen.
places.autumn_note: The Dongnae Eupseong History Festival runs Oct 16-18 2026 next door. Pleasant soaking weather.
places.cost_note: 2026 prices: adult weekday 15,000; Sat/Sun/holidays 18,000. Jjimjilbang add-on 4,000.
places.tips: Oncheonjang station (Line 1), about 10 min walk. Hotel Nongshim guests get access. Tattoos are generally tolerated in Korean bathhouses.

places.name: Spa Land Centum City (Shinsegae)
places.summary: Upscale jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse with sauna rooms) inside the world's largest department store, with 18 hot-spring baths fed by water from 1,000 m underground and 13 themed sauna rooms.
places.why: Polished bathhouse and sauna culture, an easy rainy-day choice. Still open in 2026.
places.autumn_note: Good for a rainy or chilly day.
places.hours: 09:00-22:00, last entry 21:00 (hours since 1 Sep 2026)
places.cost_note: Official: adult 26,000 every day of the week, 4-hour limit; overtime 5,000/hour; stay up to 6 h if you spend 10,000+ inside. Bring luggage-free (outside lockers 3,000 for 5 h).
places.booking: Walk in; Klook/Waug sometimes slightly cheaper
places.tips: Centum City station (Line 2). Hurshimchung is cheaper and more onsen-like; Spa Land is newer and design-led.

places.name: Ananti at Busan Cove: Water House and seaside promenade
places.summary: Clifftop resort complex with a hot-spring spa (Water House) and an infinity pool by the sea, plus the 'Ananti Town' promenade with the Eternal Journey bookstore and cafes.
places.why: The most Izu-ryokan-like spot in Busan: a seaside hot-spring soak in a calm, design-led resort.
places.autumn_note: Water House hot-spring baths with sea views suit chilly October evenings.
places.hours: Water House hours vary by season (not verified for 2026)
places.cost_note: Water House admission is separate even for hotel guests in many rate plans. Earlier prices were about 40,000-80,000 KRW; not verified for 2026.
places.booking: Via ananti.kr; non-guest access may be restricted
places.tips: Free to walk the town and bookstore. A guest shuttle from Busan Station exit 9 has run since 11 Jul 2026. Check whether your rate includes Water House.

places.name: Gijang coast: Jukseong Cathedral set and Ilgwang Beach
places.summary: A small white and red church (built as a drama set) on a rock at Jukseong-ri, plus quiet Ilgwang beach with its fishing harbours and seafood shacks.
places.why: Quiet, photogenic seaside-village feel, like the small coves near Kamakura and Hayama.
places.autumn_note: Gijang is known for anchovies (spring) and for sea squirt and conger eel. October is pleasant and uncrowded.
places.hours: Always open
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Ilgwang station on the Donghae Line; Jukseong is easiest by taxi. Combine with Haedong Yonggungsa and Ananti Cove.

places.name: Seunghaksan silver grass field
places.summary: Large field of eulalia (silver grass) on the upper slopes of 496 m Seunghaksan, with views over the Nakdong River estuary and the sea.
places.why: The autumn silver-grass experience, like Hakone's Sengokuhara, inside the city.
places.autumn_note: Peaks mid-October to early November, so late October is ideal. Best in afternoon backlight.
places.hours: Daylight
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Start from Dong-A University Seunghak campus (Hadan station area); taxi up to the campus shortens the climb.

places.name: Daejeo Ecological Park (pink muhly and cosmos)
places.summary: Riverside park with large pink muhly grass and cosmos fields in autumn.
places.why: Seasonal flower-field colour, but out of the way.
places.autumn_note: Pink muhly peaks late September to mid-October and is usually fading by Oct 20. Lower priority for this trip.
places.hours: Always open
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Gangseo-gu Office station (Busan-Gimhae light rail). Only worth it if you are already near Gimhae Airport.

places.name: Tongyeong: Hallyeosu cable car (Mireuksan), Dongpirang mural village, Jungang market
places.name_ko: 통영 한려수도 조망 케이블카 / 동피랑 벽화마을 / 통영중앙시장
places.summary: Harbour town known as 'Korea's Naples'. A 1,975 m cable car runs up Mireuksan (461 m) for island-studded views of the Hallyeo waterway; Dongpirang is a mural hillside above the harbour; Jungang market sells fish and oysters; there is also the Skyline Luge.
places.why: The best Kamakura-plus-Izu combination on the trip: harbour, hills, island views and seafood. Worth an overnight.
places.autumn_note: Fresh oyster season opens in October (peak Nov-Feb). Autumn haze is low, so island views are sharp.
places.hours: Cable car roughly 09:30-17:00/18:00 in October (2024-25 pattern); maintenance closures happen several times a year
places.closed: Some maintenance days, often a Monday; check ttdc.kr / cablecar notices
places.cost_note: Cable car adult round trip about 15,500-17,000 KRW (2024-25 level; official site blocked, so unverified). Skyline Luge about 14,000-17,000 per ride (2024-25 level).
places.booking: On site; arrive by 10:00 on weekends to avoid long waits
places.tips: Intercity bus from Busan Seobu terminal (Sasang) about 1h40-2h. Try Chungmu gimbap and kkul-ppang (honey bread). Overnight at Stanford Hotel & Resort.

places.name: Geoje: Windy Hill and Oedo Botania
places.summary: Windy Hill is a grassy headland with a Dutch-style windmill over the sea. Oedo Botania is a private island garden reached by tourist ferries, with about 1.5 h on the island.
places.why: Seaside and garden scenery comparable to Izu's coast.
places.autumn_note: Mild weather; Oedo's gardens are less colourful in autumn than in spring.
places.hours: Oedo ferries roughly 08:30-16:00; weather-dependent
places.cost_note: Ferry about 20,000-25,000 KRW round trip plus Oedo admission about 11,000 KRW (2024-25 level, unverified)
places.booking: Ferry companies at each port; foreigners can book by phone or on site. Bring a passport.
places.tips: Lower priority than Tongyeong if time is short. A car or taxi helps a lot here.

places.name: Tongdosa Temple (Yangsan)
places.summary: One of Korea's three 'Jewel' temples, founded in 646. It enshrines relics of the Buddha (so there is no Buddha statue in the main hall). UNESCO World Heritage site (Sansa).
places.why: Comparable to Kenchō-ji or Engaku-ji in Kamakura: an old, serene head temple with a forest approach.
places.autumn_note: The forest path (Muppungyosong) turns gold in late October to November.
places.cost_note: Cultural-property admission was abolished nationwide in May 2023, so entry is free (parking is paid)
places.tips: Intercity bus from Busan Nopo terminal (Line 1 terminus) to Tongdosa/Sinpyeong, about 25-30 min.

places.name: Gyeongju (from Busan)
places.summary: Former Silla capital, with royal tumuli (Daereungwon), Cheomseongdae, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at night, Hwangnidan-gil, Bulguksa and Seokguram.
places.why: The Kyoto/Nara layer of the trip. May be covered in more depth by the Gyeongju researcher.
places.autumn_note: Late October brings silver grass around the tumuli and pink muhly near Cheomseongdae; foliage at Bulguksa starts in late October.
places.hours: Varies
places.cost_note: See the Gyeongju researcher's file
places.tips: Busan Station to Singyeongju by KTX about 30 min; or ITX/Mugunghwa on the Donghae line from Bujeon or Haeundae-area stations.

lodging.name: Paradise Hotel Busan
lodging.room_for_3: Ocean-view Deluxe Double sleeps 3 (double bed plus extra bed); Deluxe Family / Twin rooms; or 2 rooms
lodging.price_note: Hotelscombined snapshot for Oct 12: from 209,425 KRW (lowest room, 2 people). Kayak shows similar October rates. Estimate for 3 in an ocean-view room with extra bed: about 350k-500k KRW on weeknights and 450k-650k on Fri/Sat. Junior suites were 823k-1.04M for a June 2026 date. Packages that include Cimer cost more.
lodging.highlights: Beachfront on Haeundae. Cimer is an outdoor sea-view hot-spring pool and spa using natural hot-spring water, the most onsen-like hotel experience in Busan. Infinity pool, casino, 9.2/10 reviews.
lodging.drawbacks: Rooms are on the small side for a 5-star. Cimer is closed on the 4th Wednesday of each month (Oct 28, outside the trip) and is not always free for guests; check the rate plan. Expensive at weekends.
lodging.booking: paradisehotel.co.kr, or OTAs (Agoda/Booking/Expedia); foreigners can book

lodging.name: Ananti at Busan Cove
lodging.room_for_3: Ocean-view rooms with extra bed, or the larger 'Penthouse' / villa-style rooms; ask for 3-adult occupancy
lodging.price_note: Hotelscombined lowest rate snapshot 182,176 KRW for 2 people; Expedia showed USD 171 for a May 2026 date. Estimate for 3 in an ocean-view room: 350k-700k KRW, weekends at the top end. Water House is often extra.
lodging.highlights: Most ryokan-like stay on the Busan coast: clifftop sea views, Water House hot-spring spa, infinity pool, Eternal Journey bookstore, a quiet design-resort feel. 5 minutes from Haedong Yonggungsa.
lodging.drawbacks: Far from the city (25-30 min taxi to Haeundae). Water House usually extra. Pricey.
lodging.booking: ananti.kr or OTAs. A guest shuttle from Busan Station exit 9 has run since 11 Jul 2026.

lodging.name: Hotel Nongshim (Hurshimchung)
lodging.room_for_3: Triple ondol room (floor bedding plus bed); a family guest reviewed the triple ondol well
lodging.price_note: Hotelscombined snapshot: from 137,976 KRW; standard rooms around 176k-280k. Estimate for a triple ondol room for 3: 180k-300k.

tips: Best fit for the Kamakura feel: base 2-3 nights in Haeundae or Gwangalli. Spend one day on Dalmaji-gil, the Sky Capsule to Cheongsapo, the Beach Train to Songjeong and Haedong Yonggungsa; one day on Yeongdo (Huinnyeoul and Taejongdae), Jagalchi, Gukje Market and the Songdo cable car; Igidae plus Gwangalli at night.
Put Busan late in the trip (e.g., Oct 21-24) so you catch the drone show on Sat Oct 24 at Gwangalli, then take a late-morning KTX to Seoul and AREX to ICN on Sun Oct 25 for the 21:55 flight.

For the onsen-ryokan analog, choose between Paradise Hotel Busan (Cimer outdoor sea-view hot spring, in the city) and Ananti Cove (Water House, quiet clifftop resort). Hotel Nongshim plus Hurshimchung is the budget onsen-town option, with no sea view.
Book the Sky Capsule the moment your date opens; weekdays are far easier. One capsule fits all 3 (55,000 KRW).
Use Naver Map or KakaoMap (Google Maps walking directions are weak in Korea) and Kakao T for taxis. A T-money card covers the metro, buses and the Donghae Line.

Budget sketch for Busan per person: 3 nights at about 350k KRW per night for 3 = about 350k each; activities (Sky Capsule + Beach Train + cable car + spa + X the Sky) about 90k; transport within Busan about 30k; KTX Seoul-Busan return about 120k. Total about 590k KRW, roughly US$410-420 at about 1,400 KRW/USD (exchange rate is an assumption).
warnings: Haeundae Grand Hotel is CLOSED (since 2018/19) and is being redeveloped. Ignore it.
Hurshimchung was closed for about 2 months of renovation in spring 2026 and reopened on 1 May 2026. Prices are unchanged at 15,000 weekday / 18,000 weekend.

Spa Land Centum is still open, but hours changed on 1 Sep 2026 to 09:00-22:00 (last entry 21:00), and the price is now a flat 26,000 KRW every day. Older guides quoting 06:00 opening or 17,000-20,000 prices are out of date.
Paradise Cimer closes on the 4th Wednesday of each month (Oct 28 2026, outside the trip).
Busan's mountain foliage (Geumjeongsan, Beomeosa) peaks mid to late November. Late October is still mostly green, so focus on the coast, silver grass (Seunghaksan) and Tongdosa's forest path.
Daejeo pink muhly is usually past peak by Oct 20.
BIFF (Oct 6-15) and the Busan Fireworks (Nov 7) both fall outside the travel dates.
Jagalchi's main building historically closes on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday (Oct 20 2026 is the 3rd Tuesday); unverified for 2026.
Sky Capsule prices posted on blogs vary (30k-50k): use the official 55,000 per capsule for 3.
